the source of tasmanitoids in the Gulf of Michigan during the last glacial maximum is the Upper Devonian black shale of the Michigan Basin.
the source-to-sinks pathway of Devonian tasmanites is from their host Devonian black shale source to the Gulf of Michigan, and then via the Mississippi River to the Gulf of Gulf of Mexico.

the source-to-sank pathway of reworked Devonain tasmanitids is a useful proxy for glacial history.
